variables.values: Integer N parsed with std::atol. N <= 0 turns hardware (FPGA) attention off for all models; non-numeric text parses as 0. N > 0 turns it on for all eligible models and also sets the engagement point.
variables.default: Unset: each model uses its compiled default, and the engagement point is token position 127. The default is on when the model plugin defines force_hw_attn = true and off otherwise; the ingest code generator emits that constant (ingest/src/TronCpp.hs:258). variables.effect: Selects whether attention runs on the FPGA cards or in software. With N > 0 it also sets the first 0-based token position of a sequence that hardware attention serves; software serves all positions below it.

So N from 1 to 127 gives 127 and N = 128 gives 255. The value is read once per process. The variable cannot force hardware attention. Each of these keeps a model in software: a pipeline stage that does not hold the embedding layer (h/tron/models/model.hpp:1791), a model shape that is not eligible or an EAGLE draft model (h/tron/models/model.hpp:1803), a hardware attention scale that the device cannot represent (h/tron/models/model.hpp:1808), no POS device (h/tron/models/model.hpp:1816), too little EMEM (the FPGA memory that holds the Q.K dot products) and an activation format that the device cannot read (h/tron/models/model.hpp:769-786). There are 14 reader lines in this area; 6 are listed. The other 8 are helper calls: hw_attn_engagement_point at h/tron/models/model.hpp:1864, :2966, :3065, :3067 and h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:2110, and use_hw_attn_for_this_model at h/tron/models/model.hpp:1817, :2891 and h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:2151. h/runtron/stream_generate.hpp:863 (outside this area) also calls hw_attn_engagement_point().

variables.values: Integer parsed with std::atoi. Non-numeric text gives 0. The unit is tokens per forward pass.
variables.default: 100000000 tokens when unset. An empty value gives 0.
variables.effect: Sets the soft limit on the number of live tokens (token jobs) that one forward pass of a scheduler takes. At the limit the scheduler stops adding tokens to the pass and records that the pass did not schedule everything.
variables.notes: When the model config has max_minibatches above 0, the limit is lowered to max_minibatches x max_minibatch_size. The field comment calls it a soft limit that can be exceeded in some cases (h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:1976): a page that already has KV work is bound only by the hard capacity limit (h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:2180-2188). The variable is read each time a scheduler is constructed; an EAGLE draft scheduler is a second scheduler and reads it again. The code does not reject 0 or a negative value. The check 'n_live_tokens >= live_token_limit' (h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:2410) is then true for the first token of every edge, so that loop adds no token to the pass. bin/analyze-tps puts the assignment in front of the runtron command that it runs on a remote host.

variables.values: Integer parsed with std::atoi. The unit is seconds between log outputs. A positive value turns the watchdog on. 0 or non-numeric text leaves it off. A negative value also starts the watchdog thread, which then logs about every 100 ms.
variables.default: Off when unset or empty.
variables.effect: Each latch arena starts a watchdog thread. Every N seconds the thread writes an info log entry 'Latch states' with the count and name of every latch in the arena.
variables.notes: A latch is a counter that threads wait on during a forward pass; each model state owns one latch arena (h/tron/models/model.hpp:1240). The watchdog thread pins itself to CPU 0 and wakes every 100 ms (h/tron/threading.hpp:225 and :230). The environment is read once; the text is converted again for each new arena. For a negative value the wait test is never true (h/tron/threading.hpp:228-231), so the thread logs at every wake-up. The source comment asks for a positive integer (h/tron/threading.hpp:174). The CMake CI workflow sets the value 60 for all its jobs.

notes: Result of the verification. The corrected list has the same 31 names as the sweep. No name was added and no name was removed. 16 entries were corrected; the other 15 match the code. Method. All 162 files of the area were searched again, independently of the sweep, for: getenv in any spelling, secure_getenv, environ, envp, setenv, putenv, unsetenv, clearenv, load_env; every identifier that contains env in any letter case; exec, spawn, popen, fork and system calls; every quoted upper-case token with an underscore; every quoted text that starts with a known prefix (TRON_, POS_, RZ_, DICE_, HF_, USE_, and others); the short standard names (HOME, TMPDIR, USER, PATH, TZ and others); library calls that read the environment (temp_directory_path, locale, hwloc, spdlog::cfg, curl, httplib); and comments that mention an environment variable. The search found 34 getenv call lines in 14 files. Every one has a literal name. No name is held in a constant or a table, and no name is built at run time. The area files contain no setenv, putenv, exec or spawn call, so there is no set_only entry. Files without a hit were searched but not read line by line. All 31 sweep entries were checked against the code: each reader and setter site was opened, and values, default, effect, when, audience, owner and role were compared with the code. A script then checked that every listed site exists and that its line holds the name or the helper call. Helpers from the scope hint that are not in this area: read_arena_allocator_env (src/system/memory.cpp:93), read_heap_shadow_env (src/system/memory.cpp:106), hwattn_env_override (src/pos/device.cpp:102) and rtm_disabled_by_env (src/system/mwaitx.cpp:40) are static functions in files outside the area list, and no area file calls them. Area files call system-layer functions whose environment reads belong to other areas, for example hardware::system::system_init (h/tron/generation/harvester.hpp:369) and hardware::system::get_kv_cache_size (src/tron/scheduler/token_cache.cpp:455). src/tronutil.cpp uses cpp-httplib with OpenSSL to reach huggingface.co. The file reads no environment variable itself. cpp-httplib is downloaded at configure time (CMakeLists.txt:299) and is not in the checkout, so any variable that it or OpenSSL reads was not determined and is not listed. Comments that name a variable: every comment in the area that names an environment variable has a matching read. Two comments name variables that other areas read: TRON_NO_RTM (src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:87) and RZ_KV_CACHE_GB (h/tron/scheduler/token_cache_policy.hpp:16). TRON_HWATTN_COMPOUND_SPLIT is read, but the code discards the result, so setting it has no effect at this commit. Audience choices that a reviewer may want to change. The three prequant cache variables (TRON_NO_PREQUANT_CACHE, POS_PREQUANT_CACHE, POS_WEIGHTS_CACHE) are marked test: the readers are in a product header, but only t/t_prequant_cache.cpp includes that header at this commit. TRON_GOLDEN_TOKENS is marked operator, because rinzler_proxy is an installed program; its README calls it a test substrate. TRON_ATTN_STATS, TRON_PERF_INTERVAL_SEC and the two TRON_SPEEDOMETER variables are marked operator (statistics, logging, tuning) and could also be seen as developer-debug. Existing documentation. h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp:50 says that TRON_AMX_DISABLE 'will be listed in the TRON environment-variable document' and cites https://github.com/positron-ai/tron/issues/4338. README.stats.md describes TRON_ATTN_STATS. README.proxy.md:278 describes TRON_GOLDEN_TOKENS. doc/model_manifest.md section 9 describes POS_WEIGHTS_DIR, POS_WEIGHTS_CACHE and POS_PREQUANT_CACHE. The setter sites in the entries are outside this area (tests, scripts, one workflow). They were found with git grep over the whole checkout, and each line was read.

changes.name: TRON_PER_USER_PROMPT_CHUNK_LIMIT
changes.detail: Three fixes. (1) The caller is stream_generation_context::loop (src/tron/generation/context.cpp:22), not generation_context::loop. (2) The sweep said only that the read site has no handler. The callers loop() are noexcept (src/tron/generation/context.cpp:22, src/tron/generation/speculate.cpp:460), so a std::stoul exception ends the process. (3) The sweep implied that every TRON binary runs the read. Only stream_generate of the full or fake scheduler starts the loop (src/tron/generation.cpp:62). rinzler_proxy and rinzler_mock define their own stream_generate (src/tron/scheduler/proxy.cpp:381, src/tron/scheduler/mock.cpp:106) and never call the helper.

changes.name: TRON_DRAFT_TREE_MAX_DEPTH
changes.detail: Added the behaviour of the values 0 and 1, which the sweep did not give. A tree with only the root has depth 1 (src/tron/generation/speculate.cpp:152), and a level is added only while the depth is below the limit (src/tron/generation/speculate.cpp:620). So 0 and 1 never extend the tree.

changes.name: TRON_DRAFT_TREE_MAX_WIDTH
changes.detail: Added a missing interaction. When the value is above 1, the initializer calls defrag_books_depth() (src/tron/generation/speculate.cpp:44). TRON_DEFRAG_BOOKS_DEPTH is then read at static initialization, not at the first extend request.

changes.name: TRON_USE_SPECULATION

changes.name: TRON_ATTN_STATS
changes.detail: Added the directory name for an EAGLE draft state. The sweep gave only /model/<model id>/attention/. The code uses attention_eagle for a draft state (h/tron/models/attn_stats.hpp:919).

changes.name: USE_HW_ATTN
changes.detail: Completed the list of conditions that the variable cannot override. The sweep left out two checks in configure_hw_attention: a pipeline stage that does not hold the embedding layer (h/tron/models/model.hpp:1791) and a hardware attention scale that the device cannot represent (h/tron/models/model.hpp:1808).

changes.name: TRON_AMX_DISABLE
changes.detail: Added a second place that turns the build option on. The sweep named only the deb preset. The CMake CI job also configures with -DTRON_AMX_DISPATCH=ON (.github/workflows/cmake-single-platform.yml:355). Also added where the result can be seen: the amx_available field of the attention stats summary (h/tron/models/attn_stats.hpp:728).

changes.name: TRON_LOG_KV_GRANULARITY
changes.detail: Sharpened the bad-value behaviour. The sweep said only that the read site has no handler. The first call normally comes from the book constructor, which is noexcept (h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1342-1376), so a std::stoll exception ends the process.

changes.name: TRON_MAX_LOGITS_CHUNK_SIZE
changes.detail: Made the behaviour for 0 and for a negative value exact. The sweep said only that the code divides by the chunk size. With 0 the chunk size is 0, and partition_listeners divides by it in every forward pass (h/tron/models/model.hpp:2058 and :2161). A negative value wraps to a very large size_t, so the chunk size is the number of pool workers.

changes.name: TRON_DEFRAG_BOOKS_DEPTH
changes.detail: Two fixes. (1) The helper call at src/tron/generation/speculate.cpp:44 is inside a namespace-scope initializer, so that read happens at static initialization, and only when TRON_DRAFT_TREE_MAX_WIDTH is above 1. The sweep listed it as a first-use read. (2) The setter count was incomplete: t/t_token_cache.cpp also restores the old value at :484 and :573, removes the variable at :486 and :575, and reads it at :411 and :494.

changes.name: TRON_PERF_INTERVAL_SEC
changes.detail: The sweep said that 0 means off and gave nothing for a negative value. The check is 'interval_sec == 0 || seconds_elapsed < interval_sec' (h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:232). A negative value is therefore not off: the line is written after every forward pass.

changes.name: TRON_LIVE_TOKEN_LIMIT
changes.detail: Made the behaviour for 0 and negative values exact. The sweep said only that the code does not reject 0. The check 'n_live_tokens >= live_token_limit' (h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:2410) is then true for the first token of every edge, so that loop adds no token to the pass.

changes.name: TRON_LATCH_WATCHDOG
changes.detail: The sweep said that any non-zero value turns the watchdog on with N seconds between outputs, and that a negative value is not rejected. For a negative value the wait test 'now - last_time < time_delta' is never true (h/tron/threading.hpp:228-231), so the thread logs about every 100 ms.

changes.name: TRON_LOG_PLACEMENT
changes.detail: Made the output form exact. The JSON is written with an indent of 2 (src/tron/hardware/placer.cpp:46), so the log entry spans several lines. The sweep called it one log line.
